sources.note: UNESCO's own programme page for the UNESCO/Japan Young Researchers' Fellowships Programme (UNESCO/Keizo Obuchi Research Fellowships Programme), last update 28 September 2026. Read in full; contains the Cycle 2026 deadline, eligibility requirements, grant details, invited Member States and research areas.

awarding_body.detail: The page is on UNESCO's own domain and is the programme's official page. It states the programme was established under the Japanese Funds-in-Trust for the Capacity-Building of Human Resources and is supported by the Government of Japan, matching the record's awarding body exactly.
awarding_body.quote: Established in 2001 under the Japanese Funds-in-Trust for the Capacity-Building of Human Resources, the UNESCO/Japan Young Researchers' Fellowships Programme, also known as the UNESCO/Keizo Obuchi Research Fellowships Programme, is a long-standing initiative supported by the Government of Japan to strengthen research capacities and promote international knowledge exchange in areas aligned with UNESCO's mandate.

deadline.detail: The page states the Cycle 2026 application deadline as 15 October 2026, midnight Paris time, and notes it has been extended, matching the record's deadline_date of 2026-10-15. The cycle is currently open (checked 12 October 2026, three days before the deadline). Letters of nomination must reach UNESCO from National Commissions by the same date, and candidates must submit to their National Commission at least 2 weeks before the deadline — both details match the record's deadline_label.
deadline.quote: Deadline for Candidate Submission is now extended to 15 October 2026. Application deadline: 15 October 2026, midnight Paris time. Letters of nomination, along with all the application documents should be submitted to UNESCO by the National Commissions no later than 15 October 2026, midnight Paris time.

eligibility.detail: All five eligibility claims in the record are confirmed on the page: nationality of an invited Member State or Associate Member (Annex 1), no more than 40 years old at the time of application, at least a Master's degree or equivalent relevant to the proposed research, proficiency in the language of instruction or supervision at the proposed Japanese host institution, and prior acceptance by an academic supervisor at a Japanese university or research institution.
eligibility.quote: Applicants must: be nationals of one of the invited Member States or Associate Members listed in Annex 1; be no more than 40 years old at the time of application; hold at least a Master's degree or equivalent in a field relevant to the proposed research and demonstrate strong academic and research potential; demonstrate sufficient proficiency in reading and writing in the language of instruction or supervision at the proposed host institution in Japan; have obtained acceptance from an academic supervisor at a Japanese university or research institution, who will oversee the proposed research.

funding.detail: The award is a lump-sum fellowship grant of up to US$10,000 intended to cover costs directly related to the research stay in Japan (international and domestic travel, accommodation, medical insurance, personal subsistence, other research-related expenses). This matches the record's 'Stipend' funding type; the record does not claim 'Fully Funded', and the page confirms the grant covers no tuition fees, equipment, publication costs or conference participation, so it is not a fully funded award.
funding.quote: Selected fellows may receive a fellowship grant of up to US$10,000. The grant will be provided as a lump-sum contribution and is intended to cover costs directly related to the approved research stay in Japan. The grant does not cover tuition fees, the purchase of equipment, including computers, publication costs or participation in conferences.

degree_levels.detail: The programme funds postgraduate research stays in Japan of no less than 3 months and no more than 9 months, beginning from February 2027 and to be completed no later than December 2027. It is a research fellowship, not a degree programme; the record's 'Postgraduate research' degree-level claim matches the page's description.
degree_levels.quote: The fellowships will support innovative and high-quality postgraduate research related to heritage conservation and management, sustainable development and artificial intelligence. Duration: No less than 3 months and no more than 9 months.
